title: Minimum Time to Collect All Apples in a Tree
summary: Given an undirected tree with vertices numbered from 0 to n-1, where some vertices contain apples, calculate the minimum time required to collect all apples starting and ending at vertex 0.
statement: Given an undirected tree with vertices numbered from 0 to n-1, where some vertices contain apples, calculate the minimum time required to collect all apples starting and ending at vertex 0. The time to traverse one edge is 1 second. The edges are defined by the array edges, and the presence of apples at each vertex is indicated by the hasApple array.
constraints: The undirected edges form a tree rooted at zero; traversing an edge costs one second.
Start and finish at zero while collecting every apple.
hints: Root the undirected tree during DFS by skipping the parent.
A child edge is needed if the child has an apple or its subtree returns positive travel cost.
Add the child cost plus two for traveling down and back.
The union of root-to-apple paths is the unique minimal subtree, and every included edge must be traversed twice.
editorial: The union of root-to-apple paths is the unique minimal subtree, and every included edge must be traversed twice.

tests.explanation: The minimal required subtree uses four edges, each traversed out and back.
Only paths to nodes two and five are retained, costing six.
